narration: The line accepts your rule: nobody moves on a guessed beat. You watch stone rise, hesitate, and then remember gravity; timber repeats the sequence half a breath later. By the third cycle you may have the real interval—or the cage’s hammering may be teaching you a false rhythm. Make an Intelligence (Investigation) check, DC 15, with advantage for observing three cycles and setting a safe abort.

success.narration: Your fourth beat lands exactly when weight becomes honest. The line pulls twice: a mason from the high window, then two children wrapped together in a curtain. On your final cutoff, the wall falls across the empty interval they just crossed. The workers keep the rhythm without you; the trapped civilians are out, and the cage remains shut.

nearMiss.narration: Your first beat is true and the line pulls a mason clear. The next interval shifts early; you cut the signal before anyone commits, and the remaining workers obey. One life is out, two windows remain unreachable, and the cage is still shut. The rescue has gained something, but the pattern will not repeat for you.

fail.narration: The fourth cycle contradicts all three before it. You cut the signal before the line moves, exactly as promised. Nobody outside is hurt—but the upper windows fold inward while everyone waits, sealing two voices behind stone. The cage’s hammering stops at the same instant, as if it had been setting the false rhythm for you.

payload.what: The madness cascade broke its apparent rhythm before the rescue line committed; two trapped voices were sealed behind the collapsed upper windows, while the caged beast stopped hammering at the same instant.
